The IND welcome the HOU as underdogs of 1.5, with the total set at 45.5 — a market that implies a HOU 24–22 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with HOU in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with HOU chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 1.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Jonathan Taylor — HOU are stingy against the run (100 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

C.J. Stroud has a passing-yards tailwind — IND allow 253 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

IND push it deep (aDOT 9.3) into a HOU defense that yields deep shots on 22% of throws — boom-or-bust upside for Alec Pierce.

Nico Collins draws a plus matchup — IND concede 68 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58). A rec-yards spot.

Dalton Schultz has room to work — IND allow 42 yds/game to TE1s (vs ~35), a receiving-yards and target angle.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it.
